research_mode: official ONS and Office for Statistics Regulation sources only; recording-quality governance, inspection, rule-change, survey-design and uncertainty gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Offence-type reliability framework
verified_claims: ONS should explain the framework used to assess reliability for different offence types
limitations: reliability can differ materially by offence

sources.name: NDQIS method disclosure
verified_claims: ONS should regularly publish NDQIS developments, methods, strengths and limitations
limitations: tool deployment does not guarantee uniform force adoption

sources.name: IT-system collaboration
verified_claims: police forces should collaborate and share knowledge to use crime-recording IT systems more consistently and efficiently
limitations: collaboration is an improvement action rather than a completed quality result

sources.name: Validation best-practice sharing
verified_claims: police forces should share knowledge on checking and validating crime records
limitations: shared practice requires local implementation and monitoring

sources.name: Multi-agency quality picture
verified_claims: Home Office, HMICFRS and ONS should combine inspection findings, management information and Home Office intelligence
limitations: no single source provides a complete current quality picture

sources.name: CSEW and recorded-crime divergence
verified_claims: ONS should work with HMICFRS, Home Office and forces to establish drivers of divergence between CSEW and police-recorded-crime statistics
limitations: divergence must not be resolved by assuming one source is always correct

sources.name: CSEW response rate
verified_claims: preliminary year-ending March 2026 CSEW response rate was 48% of the issued sample
limitations: the rate is much lower than historical levels and further non-response analysis is required

sources.name: CSEW non-response weighting
verified_claims: CSEW weights are used to adjust possible non-response bias and align the sample with the general population
limitations: weighting reduces but may not eliminate non-response bias

sources.name: CSEW Postal Address File frame
verified_claims: the face-to-face CSEW uses the Postal Address File as its sample frame
limitations: people outside private-address coverage are not represented in the same way

sources.name: CSEW 31,000-household design
verified_claims: the 2025 to 2026 sample was designed for a nationally representative 31,000-household sample

sources.name: High-crime-area sample boost
verified_claims: the 2025 to 2026 design included a 5,900-interview boost in high-crime areas
limitations: boosted sampling requires survey weights and is not a parcel inventory

sources.name: Minimum PFA interviews
verified_claims: the design targets at least 585 adult interviews in each of 42 territorial police-force areas
City of London is merged with Metropolitan Police for analysis
limitations: PFA sample minima do not support individual parcel estimates

sources.name: Complex standard errors
verified_claims: open-data tables provide complex standard errors that already account for the sample design
limitations: users should not apply an additional design factor to those supplied standard errors

sources.name: Small unweighted base caution
verified_claims: ONS recommends refraining from using estimates based on fewer than 50 respondents
limitations: small-base estimates are included only for reference and completeness

sources.name: Repeat-victimisation cut-off
verified_claims: the former cap of five incidents was replaced by a 98th-percentile cut-off from December 2018
crime-type cut-offs use three-year rolling datasets
limitations: the revised series is not comparable with bulletins published before January 2019
